content.text:
**What I took from it:** A פיקדון means you leave money in the bank for a set time, from one day to a few years, and the bank pays you ריבית. The example uses 1.8% a year, and they take 15% tax on the interest. What you give up is getting at the money. You can only take it out at the end of the period, or on certain dates if the deposit has "תחנת יציאה". If you "break" it early there's a fine, and it can eat your interest and sometimes part of what you put in. The page doesn't say how big that fine is. So I'm not putting my 30,000 there yet. I'm not very sure about any of this.

**The one thing that decided it:** The big number. 68,270 ₪ was the first figure I saw, and under it "ההפקדות שלכם 70,000". So it looked like I put in 70 and get back 68 after 10 years, which means I lose money in a deposit. There was a "בכסף של היום" button that was already selected. Maybe that's why the number is lower, but nothing next to the number said so, and I didn't press "בשקלים של העתיד".

**Where I looked, in order:**
1. The heading "פיקדון" and the line under it ("כסף שמפקידים בבנק לתקופה מוסכמת…"). That was clear.
2. The "מה זה" text. I only caught "קבועה", "משתנה" and "פיקדון לא צמוד".
3. The calculator: the big 68,270 ₪ and the chart going up in a straight line. I didn't touch my amount. The example was 10,000 plus 500 a month.
4. Scrolled past "למה משתמשים בזה" and "שווה לדעת". The only thing I saw there was "15%" tax.
5. "כסף נכנס ויוצא": "משיכה – בסוף התקופה שנקבעה בהסכם". That's the locking part.
6. "כמה זה עולה": "דמי יציאה… לפי התעריפון". No number in shekels.
7. "מיסוי": three cards. I read their headings.
8. The red box: "שבירת פיקדון לפני הזמן: האתר לא מחשב אותה. הקנס הוא תנאי של הבנק". That scared me.
9. "סיכונים": "אם בנק קורס, אין חוק שמחזיר לכם את הכסף". That was scary too.
10. The glossary at the end. I only read "קנס שבירה" and "תחנת יציאה".

**Words I didn't get:** מק"מ, "מוצרי שוק הכסף", "הבטחת קרן", "פטור למעוט הכנסה", "ריבית הפריים", "ריאלית", TXI-03 / BANK-06 and the other tags, "חשבון במערכת סגורה".

**Where I got bored:** In "מיסוי", from the paragraph about "69,840.00 ₪" and "הפסד הון". If I weren't looking for the penalty, I'd have closed the page there.

input.answer: A deposit means the bank keeps your money for a fixed time and pays interest (the example shows 1.8% a year, with 15% tax on the interest). You can only take the money out at the end, or on exit dates, and if you break it early there's a fine that the page doesn't put a number on. On top of that, the big number made it look like I'd get back less than I put in (68,270 vs 70,000), so I'm not doing it for now.
